subject: Post-call: FastPay pilot — keepalive / multiplexing proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hernandez <tom@fastpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Sep 2025 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + where we landed on concurrency/streaming

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposal so we can get a pilot scheduled:

Summary of FastPay asks (from today's call)
- Latency targets: p99 generation < 200ms; p95 < 150ms for small (<=256 token) requests
- Throughput: steady-state ~120 req/s, peak bursting to ~350 req/s for short windows
- Streaming: bidirectional streaming for chargeback detection pipelines; expect 30 avg concurrent streams, 50 peak
- Connections: application pattern maintains many long-lived WebSocket connections — you mentioned ~300–400 concurrent open sockets in production

Open items we promised to confirm:
1) Can Redwood support 300–400 open keepalive connections for the pilot, and what rate-limiting/quotas apply?
2) How should we size parallel request limits vs per-connection multiplexing?
3) Any constraints on streaming (max parallel streams per connection / proportional cost model)?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa will produce a short connection-capacity matrix for the pilot (keepalive, parallel requests, burst tokens) — she aims to share this by Monday.
- FastPay to confirm pilot dates and expected peak windows (time of day / region).
- We will prepare a pilot addendum (DocuSign) for a dedicated pilot capacity with monitoring and rollback criteria.

Attachments: none in this message — we will follow up with a capacity matrix.

Thanks,
Dev
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Tom Hernandez <tom@fastpay.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 20 Sep 2025 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + where we landed on concurrency/streaming

Dev — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few clarifications from our side:
- Streaming numbers: earlier I said 60 but after checking with infra it's closer to 30 average and 50 peak for the first month. We can provision to higher later.
- Open sockets: our mobile + edge devices keep a WebSocket per user. For the pilot we need the platform to support 400 concurrent open connections (we'll filter traffic to a smaller % in pilot, but want headroom).
- SLA expectations: we want to validate p95 < 150ms for short calls in the pilot. If Redwood can provide strict latency guarantees during pilot windows that helps procurement.

We'll review the pilot addendum once you share. For dates, we are aiming to start the pilot the week of Oct 6.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Hernandez

+1 212 555 0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hernandez <tom@fastpay.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + capacity matrix (first pass)

Tom — attaching an initial capacity matrix (conn_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a recommended pilot configuration. High-level callouts below.

Redwood recommended pilot config (initial)
- Keepalive / open connections (pilot): 200 guaranteed keepalive slots, with soft burst to 400 connections for short windows (subject to monitoring).
- Parallel requests: customer quota 300 parallel "in-flight" requests across the account. We expect to achieve lower tail latency by continuous batching + CPU/GPU isolation for this pilot.
- Streaming: support for 60 concurrent streaming sessions per model instance; recommend routing streaming traffic to dedicated instances to isolate prefix caching and KV memory.
- Burst allowance: token-bucket style burst tokens — default 1000 tokens/min; can be increased for pilot provided there's burst-control rules.

Notes and trade-offs
- Keepalive vs multiplexing: With 200 guaranteed keepalives and 300 parallel requests, we expect most clients to multiplex 2–3 parallel calls per connection. If FastPay cannot multiplex at the client, we can increase keepalives but that impacts cost and isolation.
- Latency: p95 < 150ms is achievable in dedicated pilot conditions for short requests (<=256 tokens) but p99 < 200ms will require tuned batching and priority routing during peak bursts.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model variants (quantized) if CPU/GPU pressure causes latency spikes; will be configured in rollout policy.

Next steps (ask list)
- Tom: confirm whether FastPay can multiplex at the client (suggested target: 2 calls per connection).
- FastPay: confirm pilot start week (Dev suggested Oct 6).
- Dev/Legal: we'll prepare a 4-week pilot addendum with monitoring/rollback and a pricing uplift for extra keepalive slots — draft attached (pilot-addendum-draft.docx).

Attachments included: conn_matrix_v1.xlsx, pilot-addendum-draft.docx

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Tom Hernandez <tom@fastpay.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fastpay.io>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 13:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + capacity matrix (first pass)

Marissa — thanks for the detailed breakdown and the attachments. A couple of pushbacks from infra/prod: 
- 200 guaranteed keepalives is below our comfort level. For the pilot we need 400 guaranteed open connections (we can't rely on soft bursts).
- p95 < 150ms is critical to our UX; if that's only "achievable" in tuned conditions we'll need a stronger SLA or an SLA credit if targets aren't met during pilot windows.

I've attached a short network diagram that shows our mobile topology and why we have so many persistent sockets. If Redwood requires client-side multiplexing, we'd prefer clear guidance and a short client library to make it painless.

If we can get 400 guaranteed keepalives for the pilot and an SLA gate with credits, we can sign for the Oct 6 start.

Best,
Tom

Attachment: fastpay_network_diagram.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hernandez <tom@fastpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + capacity matrix (first pass)

Tom — appreciate the frank feedback. I'll propose a path forward so we can keep momentum toward Oct 6:

Proposal (short-term bridge)
- Provision a Dedicated pilot with 400 guaranteed keepalive slots for 4 weeks. This will be a capacity exception and carries a 20% pilot uplift (covers reserved instance allocation and monitoring).
- Add a pilot SLA gate: target p95 < 150ms (short requests) during defined pilot windows (weekdays 9:00–17:00 PT). If Redwood misses the p95 target more than 2 times in the 4-week window during pilot hours, we will issue a credit equal to 10% of pilot fees (per missed week).
- Client guidance: Redwood will provide a small client helper (open-source) to enable simple multiplexing (2 calls per connection) — if FastPay opts to use it, we can dial down keepalive counts after pilot.

Action items
- Marissa: update the pilot-addendum-draft.docx to reflect the 400 guaranteed keepalive slots and SLA gate.
- Dev/Legal: prepare DocuSign for the pilot addendum (I'll route it after Marissa updates).
- Tom: confirm acceptance of the 20% uplift and the pilot hours above.

I'll escalate this path to our capacity team and approval chain now. If legal agrees, we can have a signed addendum by end of week and stand up pilot on Oct 6 as requested.

Thanks,
Dev
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
